models.name: multi_user_todo_guests
models.description:
Guest user accounts for unauthenticated visitors who have not yet registered or logged in.

Guest users are identified by temporary device tokens rather than email/password credentials. This table serves as the foundation for anonymous user sessions before they transition to registered member accounts.

Key characteristics:
- Identified by unique device tokens generated on first visit
- No authentication credentials (email/password) required
- Can transition to member accounts through registration
- All guest data is private and isolated per device
- Soft-deletable for data retention and audit purposes

Relationships:
- Has many {@link multi_user_todo_guest_sessions} (child table, FK direction: sessions → guests)
- May convert to {@link multi_user_todo_members} upon registration

plainFields.name: device_token
plainFields.description: Unique device token identifying the guest user. Generated automatically on first visit and used for anonymous session tracking before registration.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was created on first visit.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was soft-deleted. Null indicates active guest account.

models.name: multi_user_todo_guest_sessions
models.description:
Session tokens for unauthenticated guest access with temporary identifiers.

This table tracks authentication sessions for guest actors who have not yet registered or logged in as members. Each session records connection metadata (IP address, href, referrer) and temporal information (creation time, expiration time) for security auditing and session management.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link multi_user_todo_guests} (many sessions per guest)
- Stores append-only audit trail of guest login events

Behavioral notes:
- Sessions are created when guests establish temporary access
- Sessions expire automatically for security purposes
- Sessions are invalidated when guests register or log in as members
- This table is append-only and managed through authentication flows, not direct user CRUD operations

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the guest session was established.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the page where the guest session was initiated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led to the guest session initiation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest session expires.

models.name: multi_user_todo_members
models.description:
Registered member accounts with email authentication, password credentials, and profile information.

This table represents authenticated users in the multi-user todo application. Each member has a unique email address for login, a securely hashed password, and a display name for identification. Members own todo items and edit history entries, which are stored in separate tables with foreign key references to this table.

Key relationships:
- One-to-many with {@link multi_user_todo_member_sessions} for active login sessions
- One-to-many with {@link multi_user_todo_todos} for owned todo items
- One-to-many with {@link multi_user_todo_member_password_resets} for password recovery tokens
- One-to-many with {@link multi_user_todo_member_email_verifications} for email confirmation tokens

Account deletion uses soft delete (deleted_at) to preserve audit trails while preventing login access.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for authentication and account identification.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: BCrypt hashed password for secure authentication credential storage.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: User's public display name shown in the application interface.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was soft deleted. Null indicates active account.

models.name: multi_user_todo_member_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for authenticated member access with refresh rotation.

This table tracks active login sessions for registered members ({@link multi_user_todo_members}). Each session represents a single authenticated connection and stores connection metadata for security auditing and session management.

**Key Characteristics**:
- One member can have multiple concurrent sessions (e.g., mobile + desktop)
- Sessions are append-only audit trail of login events
- Expired sessions are retained for security auditing
- Supports token refresh rotation for enhanced security

**Relationships**:
- Belongs to: {@link multi_user_todo_members} (one-to-many)
- Managed through: Authentication flows, not direct user CRUD

**Security Notes**:
- expired_at is NOT NULL to enforce session expiration
- Connection metadata (ip, href, referrer) supports fraud detection
- Sessions are automatically invalidated on password change or account deletion

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_member_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged member's {@link multi_user_todo_members.id}. This foreign key establishes the relationship between the session and the authenticated member account.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the session was created. Used for security auditing and fraud detection.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the page that initiated the authentication request. Used for security auditing and session context tracking.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL from the authentication request. Used for security auditing and tracking authentication sources.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created (login time). Used for session age calculation and expiration checks.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires. NOT NULL to enforce mandatory session expiration for security. Used to validate active sessions.

models.name: multi_user_todo_member_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for member account recovery.

This table stores one-time use tokens that allow members to reset their forgotten passwords. Each token is associated with a specific member account and has an expiration time for security. Once a token is used or expires, it cannot be used again.

Key relationships:
- References {@link multi_user_todo_members} to identify which member requested the password reset
- Tokens are generated when a member requests a password reset via email
- Used tokens are marked with used_at timestamp to prevent reuse

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member account requesting password reset. {@link multi_user_todo_members.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique one-time use token for password reset verification. Generated securely and sent to member's email.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was generated.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token expires. Tokens are invalid after this time for security.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was used. Null if token has not been used yet.

models.name: multi_user_todo_member_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for new member registration confirmation.

This table stores verification tokens sent to members during the registration process. When a new member registers with an email address, a verification token is generated and sent to their email. The member must click the verification link (containing the token) to confirm their email address is valid and activate their account.

Each verification token is unique and has an expiration time. Once used, the token is marked as used and cannot be reused. Members may have multiple verification tokens if they request new verification emails before completing the initial verification.

**Key relationships**:
- References {@link multi_user_todo_members} through multi_user_todo_member_id (1:N relationship - one member can have multiple verification attempts)

**Business rules**:
- Each token is unique and single-use
- Tokens expire after a set duration for security
- Used tokens cannot be reused
- Multiple tokens may exist for the same member if they request re-sending

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_member_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged member's {@link multi_user_todo_members.id}. Links this verification token to the member account being verified.

plainFields.name: verification_token
plainFields.description: Unique verification token sent to the member's email. This token is included in the verification link and must be validated when the member clicks to confirm their email address.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification token was generated and sent to the member.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification token expires. Tokens cannot be used after this time for security purposes.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification token was successfully used to verify the member's email. Null if the token has not yet been used.

models.name: multi_user_todo_todos
models.description:
Core todo entity storing task information for member users.

This table represents individual todo items that members create to track their tasks and responsibilities. Each todo contains a required title, optional description and dates (start date, due date), completion status, and soft delete flag for trash management.

Key relationships:
- Owned by {@link multi_user_todo_members} through member_id foreign key
- Has edit history entries in {@link multi_user_todo_todo_edit_histories} for audit tracking

Business behaviors:
- Newly created todos are incomplete by default (completed=false)
- Soft delete moves todos to trash (deleted=true) rather than permanent removal
- Todos can be restored from trash by setting deleted=false
- Only the owning member can access, modify, or delete their todos

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_member_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged member's {@link multi_user_todo_members.id}. Establishes ownership of the todo item.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Required task name or title. Cannot be empty.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional task details or description. Can be left empty.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: Optional start date for the task. Can be left empty.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Optional due date for the task. Can be left empty.

plainFields.name: completed
plainFields.description: Completion status of the todo. False indicates incomplete, true indicates complete.

plainFields.name: deleted
plainFields.description: Soft delete flag. False indicates active todo, true indicates todo is in trash.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was soft deleted (moved to trash). Null when todo is active.

models.name: multi_user_todo_todo_edit_histories
models.description:
Edit history audit trail for tracking all modifications to todos.

This table maintains a complete audit log of every field change made to todo items. Each record represents a single field modification, capturing the field name, previous value, and new value. This normalized design enables efficient storage and retrieval of edit history while maintaining full change tracking capability.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to a single {@link multi_user_todo_todos} item
- Each row represents exactly one field change (key-value pattern)
- Supports edit history viewing and audit compliance requirements

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_todos_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the todo item that was edited. {@link multi_user_todo_todos.id}

plainFields.name: edit_timestamp
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this edit occurred.

plainFields.name: field_name
plainFields.description: Name of the field that was changed (e.g., 'title', 'description', 'start_date', 'due_date', 'completed').

plainFields.name: old_value
plainFields.description: Previous value of the field before the edit. Stored as string for flexibility across different field types.

plainFields.name: new_value
plainFields.description: New value of the field after the edit. Stored as string for flexibility across different field types.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.
